answer: Practically, the chain should attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because knoll only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, haven is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
